doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Musical family and Christmas lights
summary: Her grandmother taught piano; the family was musical but jazz was absent; childhood fascination with Christmas lights.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were your parents, did they contribute to your musical career? Did they want you or force you to take piano lessons?

Well my grandmother was a piano teacher so I think all — my brother, my cousins, we all went through her teaching. The only one who stuck with it was me. So that’s how it worked. But I have it, in a certain way, family, like a musical family. My dad plays some piano because his mother played piano. My mother, from her family’s side, her great grandfather was a director of an orchestra. And my mom played a little guitar. But I was lucky that I was surrounded by music. Unfortunately not really jazz because that was not — you know just was not part of the way I grew up. I mean the only jazz recording I had, it was Bing Crosby singing Christmas tunes. So that’s as far as jazz as I was exposed as a child but I kind of catched up.
You know you said before we were recording that you’re really into holiday lights and perhaps that’s it, perhaps that planted —

Yeah I know it just makes me happy. I know as a kid I used to stare at light two inches the Christmas tree lights changing color, and I could say, I’m not kidding, I could stay one hour. I was like — there was something magical about it, you know? And so now that they are cheap and they are LED and they don’t consume very much I kind of plaster my practice room. Like people that come here it’s like, “Wow it’s always Christmas here.” Yeah.
